newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets Allianz control of Hermes.
newsitem.headline: EU vets Allianz control of Hermes.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was starting a routine inquiry into the acquisition of German insurer Hermes Kredit Versicherungs AG by Allianz AG Holding.
The deal is part of a shareholdings swap between Allianz and Hermes' parent Munich Re AG, in which the latter receives Europe's largest private health insurer DKV.

The stake swap annnounced in July got a cautious welcome by the president of Germany's Federal Cartel Office, Dieter Wolf, who said in an interview with Die Zeit in August that it was not ideal but looked "tolerable".

Allianz was widely expected to reduce its strong position in the lucrative German private health market, but the solution found was not the best because of its link with Munich Re by way of crossholdings of 25 percent.
But, according to a Commission statement to be published in the EU's Official Journal, the current EU investigation only concerns the acquisition of Hermes.

The statement said the operation, which was submitted to the Commission for prior clearance, apparently fell under the EU's merger regulation which bans creation or strengthening of dominant positions. The EU's competition watchdog has about a month to clear the operation or start a full probe. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
